items.body: Register Login Penguins Reassign Rutger McGroarty By Brennan McClain | at November 1, 2026 4:00 pm Earlier this morning, the Pittsburgh Penguins announced they reassigned forward Rutger McGroarty to the AHL’s Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins. The transaction leaves the Penguins with one open roster spot since they didn’t make a corresponding roster move. It likely won’t be McGroarty’s last NHL stint, even in the near future. Not only has Pittsburgh dealt with multiple injuries through the first month of the 2026-27 campaign, but the team is open to moving some veterans from the roster via the trade market. If they do make a trade, McGroarty would likely be the first player up to fill the void. The Penguins acquired McGroarty a few years ago. The former 14th overall pick was originally drafted by the Winnipeg Jets, but refused to sign an entry-level contract with them. Instead of losing him to the free-agent market in a few years, the Jets dealt McGroarty to Pittsburgh for Brayden Yager . Unfortunately, McGroarty hasn’t gotten much playing time in the NHL. Since debuting with the Penguins in the 2024-25 season, McGroarty has scored four goals and nine points in 34 games with a -3 rating, averaging 12:41 of ice time per game. He has understandably performed much better with the WBS Penguins. Throughout his first season, McGroarty immediately became a quality secondary scorer, registering 14 goals and 39 points in 60 games with a -10 rating. The following season, McGroarty was arguably Wilkes-Barre/Scranton’s most efficient forward, finishing with 10 goals and 34 points in 30 games with a +10 rating. McGroarty added four goals and nine points in 15 postseason contests.

items.title: Jets shut out by Hurricanes’ red-hot goalie Pyotr Kochetkov
items.body: RALEIGH, N.C. — Pyotr Kochetkov ’s 26-save shutout gave him 10 straight victories to begin the season, Sean Walker scored two goals, and the Carolina Hurricanes beat the Winnipeg Jets 7-0 on Sunday. Kochetkov became the third goalie in NHL history to start a season at 10-0. Sebastian Aho, Juuso Valimaki, Logan Stankoven, Mark Jankowski and Jesperi Kotkaniemi also scored for the Hurricanes, who’ve won four in a row. Stankoven, Seth Jarvis, Nikolaj Ehlers and Shayne Gostisbehere all had two assists. Kochetkov tied Carey Price’s 10-win mark with Montreal from 10 years ago for the second-longest season-opening streak. Only Jack Campbell holds a longer season-beginning mark with 11 consecutive victories for the Toronto Maple Leafs in 2020-21. Kochetkov’s second shutout of the season pushed his career total to 13 in 135 games. The Jets have lost nine games in a row (0-7-2). Stuart Skinner, who made 12 saves, was pulled after allowing the fifth goal. Clay Stevenson stopped 13 shots in relief. Walker’s short-handed goal began the scoring 5:16 into the game. Aho’s power-play tally came during Carolina’s four-goal spree in the first 10 minutes of the second period. Stankoven’s goal at 9:09 of the second period stretched the lead to 5-0. At the time, the Jets had five total shots on goal. It’s Walker’s his first two-goal output in two seasons with the Hurricanes. Jets: Tuesday night at Montreal to end a four-game road trip.

items.body: Register Login Capitals Place Dylan McIlrath On Waivers By Brennan McClain | at November 1, 2026 1:45 pm The Washington Capitals needed to clear a roster spot after acquiring netminder Rémi Poirier from the New Jersey Devils earlier this morning. To that end, Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman said the Capitals placed defenseman Dylan McIlrath on waivers. According to beat reporter Sammi Silber, Washington is planning to keep three netminders on the roster for the foreseeable future. The Capitals recently ran into some injury troubles with starter Logan Thompson , so Poirier will give them some insurance behind Charlie Lindgren . Regardless, the acquisition of Poirier will cost McIlrath his roster spot. The former 10th overall pick of the 2010 NHL Draft is in his sixth season with the Capitals after signing as an unrestricted free agent ahead of the 2021-22 season. Despite the relatively lengthy tenure with the Capitals organization, it hasn’t come with a lot of ice time. Since the beginning of the 2022-23 season, McIlrath has skated in 43 games for Washington, tallying four assists while averaging 10:34 of ice time per game. McIlrath has also delivered 90 hits during that stretch. Although he hasn’t registered many games with the Capitals, he’s remained on the roster as a seventh or eighth defenseman. If he clears waivers, McIlrath will return to a familiar environment in the AHL. He played in 192 games for the Hershey Bears during his first three years with the Capitals organization, scoring seven goals and 32 points. Not only did McIlrath help the Bears win back-to-back Calder Cup championships in 2023 and 2024, but he was also the team’s captain.

items.title: The Everything Man: Devin Cooley's Desire To Learn Has Helped Him Improve As A Goaltender
items.summary: To say Devin Cooley doesn’t stop learning is an understatement. That’s helped the pet-saving journeyman handle a career-threatening concussion, the path to Calgary’s crease, and life itself.
items.body: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images Sergei Belski-Imagn Images The Everything Man: Devin Cooley's Desire To Learn Has Helped Him Improve As A Goaltender Ken Campbell Partner Nov 1, 2026 7:03 PM Published Nov 1, 2026 7:03 PM To say Devin Cooley doesn’t stop learning is an understatement. That’s helped the pet-saving journeyman handle a career-threatening concussion, the path to Calgary’s crease, and life itself. When Devin Cooley isn’t busy stopping pucks for the Calgary Flames or taking in a dog who survived their owner’s house burning down or walking his pet rabbit named Tito or playing the ukulele or the piano or the guitar – like Ferris Bueller, never had one lesson – he likes to unwind with a little bit of Albert Camus, David Hume or Seneca. The Younger, not The Elder. Because who among us doesn’t enjoy spending a little time with the great philosophers studying absurdism and stoicism? He draws the line at Friedrich Nietzsche, though, because, well, duh. “Nietzsche’s interesting, but he has a lot of anti-religion stuff, and I don’t know enough about religion to really give him a lot of credit,” Cooley said. “I try to stay away from the metaphysical stuff because it’s kind of like speculation, which I try to avoid.” Glad we got that out of the way. items.body: Register Login Capitals Acquire Remi Poirier From Devils By Brennan McClain | at November 1, 2026 11:45 am The Washington Capitals have acquired some goaltending depth from a division rival. According to a team announcement , the Capitals have acquired netminder Rémi Poirier from the New Jersey Devils for a 2027 seventh-round pick. Poirier, 25, was drafted 185th overall by the Dallas Stars in the 2020 NHL Draft. The Farnham, QC, native was playing with the QMJHL’s Gatineau Olympiques at the time, earning a career record of 62-46-13 with a .902 SV% and 3.06 GAA. The former sixth-round pick joined the professional ranks in the 2023-24 campaign, splitting his time between the AHL’s Texas Stars and the ECHL’s Idaho Steelheads. However, that was the last time Poirier ever played in the ECHL. He became the starting netminder for the AHL Stars last season. He played relatively well, earning a 27-19-8 record with a .912 SV% and 2.61 GAA. Unfortunately, although he’s had promising postseason performances in the past, he struggled throughout the 2026 Calder Cup playoffs. Surprisingly, the Devils claimed Poirier off waivers from the Stars ahead of the 2026-27 season. New Jersey already had Jake Allen and Nico Daws rostered, so the addition of Poirier raised some questions. Despite spending an entire month with the Devils, he never appeared in a game for them and was rarely invited to practice. After New Jersey acquired Connor Hellebuyck from the Winnipeg Jets, Poirier lost any remaining chance that he would suit up for the Devils. Hopefully, for his sake, he’ll have more opportunity with the Capitals. Washington lost third-string netminder Clay Stevenson before the season via waivers, and Poirier will likely be his replacement on the organizational depth chart.

When you’re an NHL executive – a role very few people get to be in – you never know when or how you’re going to be tested. One day, you’re settled into a particular job, and the next day, you have an even rarer opportunity – being the GM of a team. Even if you only have the ‘interim GM’ label, you’re getting a chance to make a direct impact. That’s the case with current Detroit Red Wings interim GM Shawn Horcoff. The former NHL player has been paying his dues as assistant GM under Steve Yzerman. After Yzerman’s departure in mid-July, Horcoff was given GM duties beginning in mid-September. Since then, Horcoff has been front and center as the Wings’ point man in the Dylan Larkin saga. While you may be of the opinion that Red Wings ownership has bungled Larkin’s trade demand and that Wings fans have every right to be angry with ownership, after Horcoff’s press conference on Thursday , you have to think Horcoff’s stock as an executive has risen considerably. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources TORONTO — Doug MacLean has worked nearly every job you can in the game of hockey, but he carries one accomplishment no one else has: the first employee in Columbus Blue Jackets history. The Ohio city was awarded an NHL franchise in June 1997, just over a year after MacLean, then the head coach of another recent expansion team in the Florida Panthers , led the team to a Stanley Cup Final appearance. He was fired by the Panthers 23 games into the 1997-98 season. But three months later, he was the Blue Jackets’ first-ever hire, being named general manager in February 1998. In a video interview ahead of the release of his book Game Day: The Uncensored Life of an NHL GM, MacLean said the transition from behind the bench to the front office was bizarre. “I walk in there on my first day and I’m the GM, and there’s a desk and a pad on it, and I’m thinking, ‘what the hell did I get myself into here?’” MacLean, sitting in his home in Summerside, P.E.I., told Daily Faceoff . A month into the job, MacLean told majority owner John McConnell they needed to hire a president to get things going on the business side of things. “He looked at me and said, ‘oh, you can be the president, too.’ And I’m thinking, ‘holy shit,’” he said. Karlsson and Sid seem to have some special milestone connection, as the Swedish defenseman netted an overtime game-winner on Crosby’s 1,000th career assist against the Red Wings in April 2024. items.summary: VANCOUVER -- Gavin McKenna had his first NHL homecoming Saturday -- or at least the closest thing to it when you're from Whitehorse, Yukon.
items.body: No. 1 pick of 2026 NHL Draft caps first Western Canada road trip with win at Vancouver VANCOUVER -- Gavin McKenna had his first NHL homecoming Saturday -- or at least the closest thing to it when you're from Whitehorse, Yukon. The No. 1 pick in the 2026 NHL Draft, played in front of family and friends, including his parents, when the Toronto Maple Leafs defeated the Vancouver Canucks 4-2 at Rogers Arena, a place he watched games as a kid, even though it was nearly 1,500 miles away from home. "It was cool," McKenna said. "Obviously, a lot of Leaf fans here as well, so to play in front of my family, came to a couple Canucks games growing up, so to play in that barn and play against that team was pretty cool." McKenna's first Western Canada road trip with Toronto already included stops at the Edmonton Oilers, a 7-2 win Oct. 24, where he saw flags representing the Yukon and Tr'ondek Hwech'in First Nation in the stands, and a 5-2 loss at the Calgary Flames two nights later. There was also a first visit to the Seattle Kraken, where the 18-year-old had his first two-goal game in the NHL in Toronto's 5-4 loss at Climate Pledge Arena on Oct. 28, before wrapping up the road trip in Vancouver with a suite full of family and friends wearing No. 92 Maple Leafs jerseys. Toronto (8-6-2) finished the trip 2-2-0 and McKenna had two goals and two assists amid a lot of media attention. items.title: Sunday Overreactions: Lightning, Wild can’t risk losing stars for nothing
items.summary: The Lightning and Wild find themselves in similar positions, needing to decide the best course of action with stars Nikita Kucherov and Quinn Hughes on expiring contracts. Michael Amato explores their conundrum and more in his Sunday Overreactions.
items.body: Last Friday, Connor Hellebuyck was on the move. A little over a year ago, Quinn Hughes was dealt on a Friday. So were Mikko Rantanen and Matthew Tkachuk before him. Now we’ve learned this past Friday that Nikita Kucherov doesn’t intend to re-sign with the Tampa Bay Lightning , and he has requested a trade. That news was nothing short of colossal, and it has the potential to completely reshape the balance of the Atlantic Division and the Eastern Conference. A Kucherov extension was always going to be complicated . He’s an elite player coming off a Hart Trophy in a market that has exploded, but Kucherov is also going to be 34 when this new deal kicks in, and the Lightning are known for trying to get a bargain in contract negotiations. They still don’t have a $10-million player and a Kucherov extension would blow their internal cap out of the water. However, that’s the reality of today’s NHL. There’s no putting the toothpaste back in the tube. If the Lightning won’t give Kucherov what he wants, someone else will next summer, regardless of his age. Now Julien BriseBois finds himself in a similar position to Bill Guerin, having a player unsigned beyond this season who is a critical piece of a Stanley Cup push. items.body: DENVER — Artturi Lehkonen scored twice, Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and an assist, and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Calgary Flames 5-2 on Saturday night. Martin Necas and Brock Nelson also scored, and defenceman Cale Makar had four assists for the Avalanche. Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves. Colorado has won two in a row against opponents playing on the second night of a back-to-back. The Avalanche defeated New Jersey on Wednesday and faced Calgary’s No. 3 goaltender, Arsenii Sergeev , less than 24 hours after the Flames beat Seattle. Joel Farabee and Martin Pospisil scored for Calgary. Sergeev made 29 saves in his second career start and first this season. Sergeev was recalled from the AHL when the Flames placed Devin Cooley on the injured list with a lower-body injury. Colorado was not whistled for a penalty, while Calgary took three — two on a double-minor late in the third period. The Avalanche, who lost defenceman Josh Manson for two months after he injured an ankle against the Devils, saw Nelson exit in the second when he took a shot by Makar off the side of his helmet. Nelson, who scored earlier in the period, was able to skate to the bench and down the tunnel. He returned in the third period. Nelson capped a three-goal burst in the first 10 minutes of the second that gave Colorado a 4-0 lead. Farabee scored 1:43 after Nelson’s goal, and Pospisil made it 4-2 when he scored 1:59 into the third. Lehkonen deflected Makar’s shot from the point at 4:09 to make it 5-2. Two of Blackwood's stops came after MacKinnon made it 1-0 late in the first. Blackwood made a sprawling glove save on Matt Coronato with 8.5 seconds left in the period and then stopped Farabee 12 seconds into the second.

items.summary: What Jake Evans has provided in Nick Suzuki’s absence is worth highlighting, especially considering the standard he’s set for his Canadiens teammates. Eric Engels explains how Saturday’s win showcased the impact Montreal’s veterans have made without their captain.
items.body: MONTREAL — Straight stats, no fancy stuff, here’s what Jake Evans has provided the Montreal Canadiens in Nick Suzuki’s five-game absence: two goals, three assists, a plus-11 rating, and a 55.4 per cent face-off efficiency while averaging 17:04 per game. Next-man-up stuff, indeed. Worth highlighting, no doubt. Especially considering Evans normally plays as Montreal's fourth-line centre but has elevated to set the standard for the maturity the young Canadiens are exhibiting night after night without their captain. “It’s like he always makes the right play,” said Chris Kreider after Evans made enough right plays to notch an assist, win 11 of 16 draws, and finish with a plus-4 rating in a 5-4 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins Saturday. It was Montreal’s fifth straight win since Suzuki went down with a hand injury. They had two-goal leads in the third period in all five games and executed on the details to win all five in regulation thanks to veterans like the 30-year-old Evans setting the example for players like 22-year-old Owen Beck . Phillip Danault , who played his 800 th NHL game Saturday, is another who’s been doing that. The 33-year-old has been playing close to 20 minutes a night in Suzuki’s absence but not playing any differently than he would playing 16 minutes per game from his usual (lower) slot. The forward ranks third in NHL history in goals among U.S.-born players (513) behind Tkachuk (538) and Mike Modano (561). He was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2024. Here, Roenick shares his thoughts on Tkachuk, who will be inducted into the Hall on Monday. Keith Tkachuk was one of the top three power forwards during his time, with Brendan Shanahan and Rick Tocchet . He wasn’t the prettiest player. He wasn’t the best skater. He never tried to do too much, because he didn’t have the blazing speed most superstars had. But he had all the intangibles. He made good passes at the right time. He was crafty with his hands — and elusive even — for a 6-foot-2, 235-pound man. He had these little moves that seemed to fool defensemen every time. He thrived in the most dangerous and painful areas. That tells you how smart he is. He’s not going to where the puck is; he’s going to where he knows the puck is going to be. He’s one of the all-time best in front of the net. He’s also one of the reasons USA Hockey is a superpower. It wasn’t just the talent and grit; it was Keith’s leadership. He had six points (five goals, one assist) in seven games, and the United States won a best-on-best tournament for the first time. But “Big Walt,” 6-foot-2, 235 pounds, went to the net anyway. “It was borderline abusive, to be honest with you,” he said with a laugh. “If you’re willing to pay the price in those tough areas, at the end of the day, you get results. There it was, he thought. His mom was giving him a helping hand. As DiPietro said later, “Definitely a good, friendly bounce there, and it wasn’t just by happenstance.” Back home, in Amherstburg, Ontario, the idea was much the same. items.summary: Nobody promised wins. But the Vancouver Canucks are finally starting to deliver on the effort and competitiveness they pledged as a baseline.
items.body: VANCOUVER – Nobody promised wins. But the Vancouver Canucks are finally starting to deliver on the effort and competitiveness they pledged as a baseline. Their 4-2 loss Saturday to the Toronto Maple Leafs dropped the Canucks to 3-12-1, which is grotesque and worse than anyone expected even for the start of a National Hockey League rebuild. But they had their goalie out and pressing for a late tying goal, as they did in Thursday’s 3-2 road loss to the San Jose Sharks, and the Canucks didn’t drown at five-on-five against another superstar-driven team. And even though Vancouver’s poor middle period decided the game, the two shots that allowed Toronto to go ahead 3-1 could have been handled better by goalie Leevi Merilainen. After getting outshot in 12 of their first 13 games, which included a 10-game losing streak, the Canucks have now narrowly outshot their opponents in three straight contests. Shots on Saturday were 29-28. It is sobering that these last three games, a 6-5 overtime win against the Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday followed by the goalie-out losses against the Sharks and Leafs, probably constitute a “hot streak” at this stage for the NHL’s worst team. But at least there is progress, which was difficult to find through most of October – a month that was Halloween for the Canucks from start to finish. “Getting closer,” coach Manny Malhotra said Saturday night. “It's not close to where we need to be or need to get to, but there is progress there. It's frustrating as we talk about these games after loss after loss, but we do see improvement in different areas of our game. It's just... tough to see those when there's no correlation to wins.” “Obviously, the end result has to change somehow,” Canucks winger Paul Cotter , part of an effective fourth line, told Sportsnet.

items.title: Kucherov would consider trade to Maple Leafs or Canadiens
items.body: The reigning MVP could have his eyes on the Atlantic Division. The Toronto Maple Leafs and Montreal Canadiens are two teams that Nikita Kucherov would consider as trade destinations, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported during Saturday Night Hockey . Kucherov has a modified no-trade clause, meaning he can submit a list of 10 approved teams he can be traded to. The Russian forward has a 10-team list, but the teams on it are currently unknown, Friedman added. This latest development comes after Kucherov informed both his teammates and the Lightning organization that he will not be re-signing with Tampa Bay and would like to be traded. There was a meeting between Kucherov, his agent Dan Milstein, head coach Jon Cooper, and GM Julien Brisebois on Friday, but they were unable to settle the situation, Friedman reported. The Lightning released a statement saying they would not be trading Kucherov. "We are aware of the media reports regarding the future of Nikita Kucherov with the Lightning," Brisebois said in a statement. "We unequivocally have no intention of trading Nikita." Kucherov, 33, is in the final season of an eight-year, $76-million contract and had 130 points (44 goals, 86 assists) last season in his second Hart Trophy-winning campaign. Friedman's reporting also included that Kucherov initially wanted his contract to be in the same territory as Kirill Kaprizov's deal, but that changed after Leo Carlsson's off-season offer sheet. However, the biggest catalyst in Kucherov's decision was the lack of pace in the negotiations.

items.title: Red Wings’ Dylan Larkin may alter trade list
items.body: Another chapter could be coming to the Dylan Larkin saga in Detroit. After making the decision on Thursday to sit out until the Red Wings fulfill his trade request, Larkin might adjust the list of teams that he is willing to waive his no-movement clause for. "He has a 10-team trade list that he's willing to go to," Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman said on the latest Saturday Headlines segment. "I think over the next 24-to-48 hours, it's possible we see that trade list altered." Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press reported on Oct. 20 that Larkin's trade list includes the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. When Larkin initially requested a trade out of the Motor City, it was reported that he was only open to a move to the Panthers, Wild and Golden Knights. But now that Larkin has opted out of playing with the Red Wings after scoring two goals and six points over 10 games, the club's former captain appears ready to find a spot outside some of the premier American NHL destinations. "Some teams like Florida and Vegas, even Colorado, it's very hard to see (a trade) happening, if not impossible," Friedman said Saturday. "So, I do think it's possible that Larkin may take some teams off, or possibly even add some teams on." Larkin was suspended without pay and taken off the roster by Detroit after the 30-year-old centre informed the team he would no longer play for the franchise. Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff said Thursday his goal is to acquire players that can help right away, adding he's open to deals for prospects and draft picks that give the franchise a fair return for someone of Larkin's calibre.

items.title: Penguins’ Crosby breaks record for most assists on a single team in NHL history
items.summary: Sidney Crosby added another honor to his historic career on Saturday night against the Montreal Canadiens.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Sidney Crosby continues to rack up NHL records and milestones. On Saturday, the Pittsburgh Penguins forward surpassed Ray Bourque for the most assists with a single NHL franchise, with a pair of assists in the first two periods against the Montreal Canadiens. The two assists, first on the opening goal to Erik Karlsson, and later on the 2-2 goal to Tommy Novak, brought him to a total of 1,112, passing Bourque’s 1,111. Wayne Gretzky, despite holding the record for the most assists in NHL history with 1,963, posted only 1,086 of those with the Edmonton Oilers , the team he spent the longest with. Rounding out the top five on the all-time assists-with-one-team leaderboard are Steve Yzerman, with 1,063 assists for the Detroit Red Wings , and Mario Lemieux, with 1,033 assists with the Penguins. Crosby’s first Saturday assist came as the primary to Karlsson’s goal, with Novak providing the secondary assist, bringing him to 100 career NHL assists. Meanwhile, Crosby now has 657 goals and 1,112 assists for 1,769 points in 1,433 regular-season games. In addition, Crosby has netted 72 goals and 134 assists for 206 points in 186 Stanley Cup Playoff games. The latest accolade comes in what has already been a history-making season for Crosby. Lining up alongside Kris Letang and Evgeni Malkin, the trio became the longest group of three to play on a single team , hitting 21 consecutive seasons, and amassed the most wins by a trio together, with 494 on Sept. 30. While Crosby’s point total has been slow to come by at 39 years old, with three goals and four assists for seven points in 13 games heading into the matchup with the Canadiens, he will be hoping for an uptick in production as the Penguins continue through the fall. items.title: Penguins’ Sidney Crosby sets NHL record for assists with single franchise
items.body: Sidney Crosby 's Hall of Fame resume grew a little longer on Saturday. With a first-period helper on Erik Karlsson's power-play goal against the Montreal Canadiens, Crosby set the NHL record for assists recorded with a single franchise. The assist was the 1,112th of Crosby career — all of them coming over his 22 seasons with the Pittsburgh Penguins . He surpassed the previous record holder, Ray Bourque, who racked up 1,111 assists over his 21 years playing for the Boston Bruins. With his 1,112 apples, Crosby sits seventh on the all-time NHL leaderboard, 23 behind Paul Coffey. Wayne Gretzky is the career leader at 1,963. Crosby is off to a slow start by his standards in 2026-27, but now has three goals and five assists through the first 14 games of Pittsburgh's season. items.title: Tage Thompson scores twice in Sabres’ win over Kings
items.summary: Tage Thompson scored twice, including the go-ahead goal with 6:20 remaining, and the Buffalo Sabres beat the Los Angeles Kings 3-2 on Saturday to extend their road point streak to seven games.
items.body: LOS ANGELES — Tage Thompson scored twice, including the go-ahead goal with 6:20 remaining, and the Buffalo Sabres beat the Los Angeles Kings 3-2 on Saturday to extend their road point streak to seven games. Jack Quinn had a goal and an assist, Zach Benson and Rasmus Dahlin each had two assists, and the Sabres won their third straight overall. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 27 saves. Corey Perry had a power-play goal, Andre Lee also scored and Anton Forsberg stopped 28 shots for the Kings. Thompson put the Sabres back in front on a one-timer off a pass from Quinn on a power play at 13:40 of the third period. Buffalo had controlled long stretches of the game before allowing the Kings to get back into it by taking some unnecessary penalties. Buffalo controlled the first period but only led 1-0 on Quinn’s eighth goal when he scored on a power play at 6:35. Even with Los Angeles gaining momentum in the second half of the second period, the Sabres made it 2-0 on Thompson’s ninth with 4:22 left. Perry got the Kings on the board on a power play with 2:36 to go, though they needed a coach’s challenge to overturn a goaltender interference call. Lee tied it 1:29 into the third. The Kings were without top forward Adrian Kempe, who is day to day because of an undisclosed injury. Martin Chromiak made his NHL debut, taking Kempe’s place on the first line and the power play.

items.body: ELMONT, N.Y. — On Halloween day, the Edmonton Oilers came dressed as the 1995 New Jersey Devils. The Oilers simply smothered a tired New York Islanders team Saturday on Long Island, constricting New York in a 4-0 win — their second straight one as Edmonton strings together six consecutive periods of perfect defensive hockey. At 10-2-2 thus far in the 2026-27 season, Edmonton continues to win games with their defensive play, a trait that has been mostly foreign to the McDavid era in Edmonton. “That was a good team to test that against because they throw everything to the slot,” said defenceman Ryan Shea, who quietly played 22:35 Saturday. “They had nine shots (on goal) through the first two periods and we were doing our jobs. That's what we’ve got to be day in, day out. Speaking of a good spot, how’s the view from the goal crease? Surely, it’s seldom been better, considering the last time Edmonton recorded back-to-back shutouts was Mike Smith in April of 2022, and before that Cam Talbot way back in 2017. “Guys are just committed,” said Tristan Jarry , who faced 24 shots in that 4-0 win over Calgary and just 18 more against the Isles. “They've really bought in from the start of training camp. They’ve added one on the back end as they’ve recalled blueliner Quinton Burns from AHL Springfield, per the NHL’s media site. It’s the first career NHL recall for the 21-year-old. Burns was a third-round pick back in 2023 out of OHL Kingston, spending two more seasons with the Frontenacs after being selected. In 2024-25, he had a big season there, tallying 49 points and 100 penalty minutes in 66 contests. That production didn’t carry over to his first professional campaign last season. Burns split the year between the Thunderbirds and ECHL Florida. With the former, he had five assists and 92 penalty minutes in 31 games while with the latter, he collected six points and 17 penalty minutes in 16 appearances. This season, Burns has an assist and 29 penalty minutes through seven outings in Springfield. At first glance, it seems unlikely that Burns will see much action. Theo Lindstein , one of their top defensive prospects, could be back up before long after getting some game action in with the Thunderbirds; he made his season debut with them last night. For now, at least, Burns will get a chance to make an impression on the coaching staff in the hopes of making his NHL debut.

items.title: Matt Pavelich, first linesman in Hockey Hall of Fame, dead at 92
items.body: NEW YORK — Matt Pavelich, the first linesman inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame, has died. He was 92. Pavelich officiated games in 19 consecutive Stanley Cup Finals from 1961-79 as part of his 23 seasons working in the NHL. He took part in 1,727 regular season and 245 playoff games during that stretch before serving as the league's supervisor of officials and going into the Hall in 1987. Commissioner Gary Bettman called Pavelich a true icon of the profession. “No linesman in the history of the National Hockey League was more universally respected nor more widely admired than Matt Pavelich,” Bettman said in a statement. “Pavelich personified professionalism and integrity while possessing a warm personal touch that enabled him to develop working relationships with players and coaches.”

Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman reports ( Twitter link ) that the Ducks have placed blueliner Nick Jensen on waivers today. With Anaheim losing a big chunk of their back end from last season ( John Carlson , Jacob Trouba , Radko Gudas , and Olen Zellweger ), the Ducks inked the 36-year-old to a two-year, $4.5MM contract on the opening day of free agency back in July. While they were planning to have some of their younger players (such as Tristan Luneau and Noah Warren ) take on full-time roles, the hope was that Jensen would be able to bring some veteran stability to their group and play some important defensive minutes. But things haven’t quite gone to plan. Jensen has found himself a healthy scratch rather often this season, getting into just three of 13 games thus far. While he has chipped in offensively with a goal and an assist in those outings, Jensen is logging just 15:20 per night, well below his career average of 18:40 with some underlying numbers that aren’t exactly making a case for him to see a bigger role. items.title: Opinion: Unlike Hellebuyck And Larkin, Nikita Kucherov Is Doing The Lightning A Solid
items.summary: Nikita Kucherov shocked the NHL by requesting a trade from the Tampa Bay Lightning, but unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, he is doing his team a solid by doing so.
items.body: James Guillory-Imagn Images James Guillory-Imagn Images Opinion: Unlike Hellebuyck And Larkin, Nikita Kucherov Is Doing The Lightning A Solid Ken Campbell Partner Oct 31, 2026 4:54 PM Published Oct 31, 2026 4:54 PM Nikita Kucherov shocked the NHL by requesting a trade from the Tampa Bay Lightning, but unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, he is doing his team a solid by doing so. Wow, this one is seismic. Among the superstars in the NHL who are asking/demanding they be moved, there's probably not a person in hockey who had Tampa Bay Lightning star Nikita Kucherov on their bingo card. With 13-plus seasons, two Hart Trophies, two Art Ross Trophies, two Stanley Cups, and more than 1,100 career points as the franchise’s leading scorer, Kucherov looked like as sure a bet as you could find to finish his career with the team that drafted him. More Videos But, unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, Kucherov is actually doing his team a favor with his public declaration. For so many reasons, this is different than the other two. And when the dust settles and emotions subside, the Lightning are going to be happy Kucherov greased his own skids out of town.

items.body: Broadcasting icon's legendary calls include 'Golden Goal' for Canada at 2010 Olympics Chris Cuthbert grew up listening to Foster Hewitt and never imagined he would one day be receiving the Hockey Hall of Fame media award named after the legendary Canadian broadcaster. Cuthbert, this year's recipient of the Foster Hewitt Memorial Award for his outstanding contribution to broadcasting, will be honored at the Hockey Hall of Fame media luncheon in Toronto on Nov. 9. "It's overwhelming and it's the ultimate honor for an NHL broadcaster for sure," the 69-year-old told NHL.com. "I may be one of the last of the recipients who grew up listening to Foster Hewitt. He was the first guy to set the dream in motion. I'd go to bed at night with Foster Hewitt on the radio under the pillow listening to him." Cuthbert has become a Canadian broadcasting icon in his own right as the play-by-play voice for a generation of hockey fans. His call of Sidney Crosby 's overtime winner against the United States at the 2010 Vancouver Olympics has been compared to that of Hewitt's in Game 8 of the 1972 Summit Series when Paul Henderson scored the winning goal for Canada against the Soviet Union. Cuthbert was 15 when Hewitt famously exclaimed, "Here's a shot, Henderson made a wild stab for it and fell. Here's another shot, right in front, they score! Henderson has scored for Canada!" More than 37 years later, Cuthbert had a famous line of his own: "Crosby scores! Sidney Crosby, the golden goal and Canada has a once-in-a-lifetime Olympic gold!" Like Hewitt's famous call, Canadian hockey fans remember where they were listening to Cuthbert in the gold medal final. items.title: Reeling Jets fall to Panthers for eighth straight loss
items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Anton Lundell had a hat trick, Seth Jones capped a record-setting month with a goal and two assists, and the Florida Panthers topped the reeling Winnipeg Jets 5-2 on Friday night for their sixth win in eight games. Jones finished October with 18 points — two goals and 16 assists — to break the record for most points by a Florida defenseman in any month. Keith Yandle had 17 points for the Panthers in March 2018. Kyle Connor had his team-best 11th goal for Winnipeg, which dropped both ends of a home-and-home with Florida this week and is winless in its last eight games — going 0-6-2 in that span. Morgan Barron had his first goal of the season midway through the third to get the Jets to 3-2, but Lundell's second of the night restored Florida's two-goal edge. Lundell finished off the hat trick — Florida's fifth already this season — with an empty-netter with 1:39 left. Akira Schmid stopped 22 shots for Florida, which remains without standout forwards Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand because of injuries. Both resumed skating this week; Marchand could be back in about three weeks and Barkov in about four, Panthers coach Paul Maurice said. Florida's Bokondji Imama and Winnipeg's Tyrel Bauer brawled just 2:04 into the game, a reenactment of sorts of their still-talked-about fight in the AHL in 2024. They went at it for more than a minute Friday and — similar to what happened at the end of their fight two years ago — shared a respectful nod toward the other when it was over. The Panthers entered Friday having played only three home games this season, the fewest in the NHL. More than half the league had logged at least seven home games going into the day.

items.title: Hellebuyck helps Devils over Golden Knights for second straight win since trade
items.summary: Connor Hellebuyck stopped 19 shots, Arseny Gritsyuk and Jack Hughes each scored twice and the New Jersey Devils beat the Vegas Golden Knights 5-2 on Friday.
items.body: LAS VEGAS — Connor Hellebuyck stopped 19 shots, Arseny Gritsyuk and Jack Hughes each scored twice and the New Jersey Devils beat the Vegas Golden Knights 5-2 on Friday. Hellebuyck, who spent his first 11 seasons in the NHL with the Winnipeg Jets, had his second win since the Devils acquired him Oct. 23 . The three-time Vezina Trophy also was in goal Tuesday night in Dallas in a 5-1 win. Gritsyuk has scored at least a goal in six of the last eight games and has 10 points during the stretch. Luke Hughes also scored for New Jersey. The Devils improved to 10-1-0 when the Hughes brothers score in the same game. Mark Stone and Ivan Barbashev scored for the Golden Knights, and Adin Hill stopped 26 shots. Luke Hughes got things going early in the first when he rifled a one-timer from the top of the left circle past Hill. Stone tied it when he deflected Mitch Marner’s blast from the point past Hellebuyck. Barbashev gave the Knights a 2-1 lead moments later when he tapped Marner’s pass home after a picture-perfect cross-crease pass. The lead didn’t last one minute, as Gritsyuk took advantage of a turnover and sniped Hill top shelf from the left circle. Jack Hughes put New Jersey back in front when he stole the puck from Jack Eichel in the neutral zone, then passed it to himself through Stone’s legs before beating Hill. Gritsyuk scored his second goal by backhanding his rebound after Hill blocked his first attempt.

Type of Challenge: Puck Out of Play
Result: Call on the ice is upheld
Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if,
items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” After a thorough examination of all available replays, there was no conclusive evidence that the puck shot by Florida’s Dmitry Kulikov at 12:03 (7:57 elapsed time) was deflected before going out of play . Therefore, the call on the ice stands. The decision was made in accordance with Rule 38.2 (d) which states, in part, that a team may request a Coach’s Challenge “When a minor penalty for delaying the game has been assessed under Rule 63.2 (iii) for shooting or batting the puck out of play from the defending zone. This will only apply to delay of game penalties when the shot/batted puck is determined to have subsequently deflected off a player, stick, glass or boards, etc., and not a judgment call.” Therefore, an additional minor penalty was assessed to Florida (in addition to the existing delay of game penalty).

items.title: Senators’ Hodgson suspended two games for boarding Kings’ Clarke
items.body: Hayden Hodgson will be watching the next two games from the press box. The Ottawa Senators forward has been suspended for two games for boarding, the NHL's Department of Player Safety announced Friday. The punishment comes after Hodgson received a game misconduct and major penalty for boarding Los Angeles Kings defenceman Brandt Clarke on Thursday night. Hodgson took a run at Clarke, charging in at 21 m.p.h., according to the game broadcast. Clarke was just below the goal line when he was driven into the boards. The hit caused a brief scrum, and the Kings' Erik Haula received a two-minute penalty for roughing Hodgson. Clarke was ruled out for the rest of the game for what the Kings called an upper-body injury. The play with 8:45 left in the second period came shortly after the Kings scored three goals in 4:03 to take a 4-1 lead and chase goalie Jonas Johansson. Hodgson has played in only 24 NHL games over five seasons, but including Thursday, has amassed 51 minutes in penalties. Hodgson was fined $2,018, the maximum allowed under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement, in October 2025 for boarding Montreal's Alex Newhook in a pre-season game. He has a long history of suspensions — 20 games worth — in the American Hockey League for elbowing and other offences over the past five seasons. He’ll forfeit $8,763 in salary as a result of the suspension. He'll miss games Saturday at San Jose and Sunday at Anaheim. He's eligible to return Wednesday at Buffalo. The Senators recalled wingers Xavier Bourgault and Philip Tomasino from Belleville of the AHL. The Senators continue their West Coast road trip at San Jose on Saturday and at Anaheim on Sunday.

items.body: VANCOUVER — The last time Leevi Merilainen had the stage to himself, the goalie stepped through a trap door and fell all the way back to the minors. With the Vancouver Canucks , the 24-year-old is coping better with the spotlight, as unexpected as that bright beam has been. Claimed on waivers from the Ottawa Senators just before the season began, Merilainen has so badly outplayed veteran goalie Kevin Lankinen that the prospect has started six of the last eight games, including three straight. It is Merilainen’s longest run of National Hockey League games since the Senators, desperate for saves after Linus Ullmark’s personal leave of absence last season, forced their rookie to start 11 straight games in December and January. Merilainen admitted things “didn’t go as well as I wanted” and spent the rest of last year back in the American Hockey League after the Senators signed James Reimer mid-season. As Vancouver starter Thatcher Demko ’s rehab from major hip surgery last February drags on, the Canucks are certainly not looking at ways to replace Merilainen. They’ve actually got to be careful not to overplay him. “It's definitely a part of the conversation,” head coach Manny Malhotra said Friday, after the Canucks practised for Saturday’s home game against the Toronto Maple Leafs. “At the same time, that's a part of growth — learning to take on more minutes, learning to take on more responsibility. The Russian winger is arguably the greatest player in team history, recently passing Steven Stamkos as the franchise’s all-time points leader. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images Two-time Stanley Cup champion and reigning Hart Memorial Trophy winner Nikita Kucherov has requested a trade from the Tampa Bay Lightning, Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman reported Friday evening. Kucherov, 33, has four goals and 15 points in 12 games with the Lightning to start the 2026-27 regular season. According to Friedman, Kucherov has notified both Lightning management and his teammates that he does not intend to re-sign with the club. “The exact reasons are unclear at this point, but Kucherov — the NHL’s reigning MVP — is in the final season of an eight-year, $76-million contract.
